Wing 38 · Passersby

Everyone the diary remembers,
and where it met them.

Six character diaries hold the world instead of the character: 3,933 player cards with class, race and level; 4,152 positional sightings across 18 maps; 494 contacts on an interaction tape; and 4 dungeon dockets with the loot rolls still inside. The window is 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-24 — fifteen days of other people.

01The ledgerwhat the six diaries hold, counted once, never estimated

A diary here is not prose. The addon keeps four tapes: characters (one card per player it ever resolved), sightings (position, map, sub-zone, and how it saw them), interactions (a typed contact) and instances (a dungeon docket with its loot rolls). Everything on this page is read out of those four tapes and nothing else — no name is invented, no zone is guessed.

Six diaries, one crowd. Every character folder carries its own social_diary.lua; the builder merges them by GUID, so a player seen by two of my characters is one soul with the widest window, not two. Cards: 3,933. After merging: 3,933. The difference is the overlap the merge removed.

02The crowdclass, race, faction and level of everyone the nameplates resolved

Classes are painted in the client's own RAID_CLASS_COLORS, so the page reads like a raid frame. 3,878 souls carry a level: min 1, median 24, max 60, and 29 of them at the level-60 cap. The server's custom race token Skyborne is kept verbatim — relabelling it would be a claim the data does not make.

03The streetseach dot is one sighting at the observer's own map coordinates; colour is the class of the soul standing there

The diary stores raw normalised map coordinates, so the sightings can be plotted without a single external map asset. Bright dots came from a nameplate, dim ones from a tooltip hover. The clustering is not decoration: it is where the crowd actually stands — the bank steps, the flight master, the inn door. The twelve busiest maps appear here; the full sub-zone table follows.

04The clockwhen the world was crowded, in station time

05The regularsthe 228 souls the diary met more than once, or an hour apart

Two sightings, or one sighting and another an hour later, is someone the diary can say it knows: the same GUID, a window between first and last, and a count of how often it crossed my path. This is the closest thing to a friends list that the tape contains — the addon never records an actual friend flag.

06The interaction tape494 typed contacts between 298 souls and my characters

The tape is typed, not narrated: level_up means someone dinged in front of me, campfire that we shared one, saved_you that someone pulled me out of a death, tried_to_help that they tried and it did not land. Five kinds of contact exist exactly once or twice in the whole window — those rows are the page's real content, so they are listed in full rather than summarised.

07Dungeon dockets4 runs, 21 bosses, 71 loot rolls — who won what

Each docket is one instance run with its pauses, deaths, wipes and every loot roll inside it: the item link (decoded, quality colour preserved), the winner resolved through the same card table, and how many others rolled need. The docket carries no instance name — so this page prints the boss roster and refuses to guess the dungeon.

08The six diariesthe same file also keeps a sheet per character: what I survived, not who I met

The last tape is my own. Each journey sheet records route segments, deaths, kill-grinds, campfires and — the sharpest rows in the whole ledger — close calls: the health percentage that was left, how many foes it was against, and how many seconds the character held out. Deaths and levels are counted elsewhere on the station; the close calls are counted nowhere else. The account scope of the same addon (SocialDiaryDB, v4.2.4) resolves each sheet to a real name and keeps its own played counter at 63.8 h across 37 sittings.

account scope: my own roster, settings, played counter
Method. Generated, not hand-typed. passersby_extract.py finds the station by walking up until Wow.exe appears, globs every WTF\Account\**\social_diary.lua, and parses each with the station's own strict Lua reader (microdeeds_extract.LuaParser) — the same reader the Deeds wing uses, so a grammar drift raises instead of quietly producing zeros. Cards are merged by GUID (widest window wins, name lists union); sightings are de-duplicated on (time, x, y, mapID); interactions on (type, time).

Names are resolved from the card's own names list, taking the newest entry, so a rename inside the window cannot invent a person. Items are decoded from the hyperlink (|cnIQ<q>:|Hitem:<id>) and painted in the client quality colours; dungeon name, guild and friend status are never inferred. Clocks are unix epoch seconds rendered at UTC−5, the offset InkAndEmbers.lua stores for this account; nothing is converted silently.

Nothing was deleted to build this page. Regenerate with python Dark_Portal\Timeline\passersby_extract.py — it rewrites _gewey_gui\Passersby.html, mirrors Timeline\data\passersby.json, and copies the previous render into _gewey_gui\.history\ first. --check parses and reports without writing; --json stops after the payload.
